HomePage.title: UPolníček
HomePage.tagline: A system for submitting student work, grading it, and keeping track of deadlines.
HomePage.what: A teacher creates an assignment with a deadline and a number of points; a student submits work to it. Programming assignments are compiled and run in a sandbox against prepared tests, with a result in seconds. Work a machine cannot judge — documents, data, presentations — is collected against the same deadline and graded by the teacher. Points, feedback and the history of attempts all stay with the submission they belong to.

groups.title: Groups
groups.body: Groups organise teaching into self-contained units — a course, a lab, a competition. They form a tree, so a course can hold its own lab groups and whoever administers the course administers those too. Every group has members, assignments and its own rules for points.

exercises.title: Exercises
exercises.body: An exercise is a template made of two main parts: the text of the task, and the set of rules a submission is judged by. For programming exercises the author can set tests, limits on the resources a solution may use, and automatic grading. For other exercises the checking and the points are the teacher's own.

solutions.title: Solutions
solutions.body: A student submits files or an archive. Programming assignments are compiled, run against every test, and reported with what passed, what the compiler said and how close to the limits the solution ran; other work is recorded and left for the teacher to judge. Teachers see every attempt, can comment on the submitted text line by line, and can override the points.

deadlines.title: Deadlines and the calendar
deadlines.body: Every assignment has a submission deadline, the maximum points available and optionally a second deadline worth fewer of them. A student's overview holds a month calendar of all their submission deadlines. A teacher sees the same for the courses they teach, plus the group's matrix of points and the queue of solutions waiting to be looked at.

notes.regex-comparison: Its comparison is a regular expression, which no judge here can do. Nothing was created for it.

notes.framework-run: Its run command hands the decision to a test framework, which cannot become a stdin/stdout pair. It could be one test judged on the exit code, but that turns a whole suite into one pass or fail, so nothing was created for it.
notes.no-input-or-output: It declares neither input nor expected output, so there is no pair to carry. Nothing was created for it.
notes.setup-command: Its setup command was dropped — there is nowhere here to run one. The language's runtime has to already provide whatever it installed.

notes.unnamed-test: It has no name, so it was named after its position.
notes.renamed-test: Its name uses characters UPolníček does not allow in a test name, so it was rewritten.

tests.title: Tests
tests.explain: Every test is run against the submitted solution, and the student's score is worked out from the rules below.

calculatorsExplain.uniform: The correctness is the plain average of the test results.

calculatorsExplain.universal: The score is a custom expression over the test results — a test that has to pass before the others count, say.

config.stdinFileExplain: The chosen file is fed to the program on standard input.
config.runArgsExplain: Passed to the solution on its command line.

judges.recodex-judge-float: Token by token, numbers compared approximately
judges.recodex-judge-normal-newline: Token by token, ignoring line ends
judges.recodex-judge-float-newline: Token by token, numbers approximate, ignoring line ends
judges.recodex-judge-shuffle-all: Tokens and rows in any order
judges.recodex-judge-shuffle-newline: Tokens in any order, ignoring line ends

config.entryPointExplain: The file to start. Left unset, the submitted file is started.
config.successExitCodes: Exit codes that count as success
config.successExitCodesExplain: Single values or ranges, separated by commas — for example 0, 2-4.
config.extraFilesExplain: These join the submitted files before compilation — headers, modules or libraries the solution would not build without. Unlike the input files above they are not the test's data but part of what is compiled, and they are set per language.
config.jarFilesExplain: Jars put on the class path.
config.execTargetsExplain: Which targets the build tool runs.
config.expectedOutputRequired: Without an expected output the test cannot be judged and the exercise cannot be assigned.

judgeExplain.recodex-judge-normal: Compares token by token. Whitespace does not matter; the order of the tokens and the split into lines does.
judgeExplain.recodex-judge-float: Like token by token, but numbers are compared as numbers — a small rounding difference passes.
judgeExplain.recodex-judge-normal-newline: Like token by token, and where the lines end does not matter — a newline is just more whitespace.
judgeExplain.recodex-judge-float-newline: Numbers are compared as numbers and the line ends do not matter.
judgeExplain.recodex-judge-shuffle: Tokens on one line may come in any order; the order of the lines has to match.
judgeExplain.recodex-judge-shuffle-rows: Lines may come in any order; within a line the order has to match.
judgeExplain.recodex-judge-shuffle-all: Neither the order of the lines nor the order of the tokens in them matters.
judgeExplain.recodex-judge-shuffle-newline: Tokens in any order, and the line ends do not matter.
judgeExplain.diff: The files have to match exactly, byte for byte, whitespace and line ends included.

ExerciseScore.title: Custom scoring
ExerciseScore.explain: Instead of an average, the correctness of a solution can be any expression over the test results — a test that must pass before the others count, a bonus that is capped, a part of the exercise weighted to nothing.
ExerciseScore.syntax: A test result is its name in quotes and is a number from 0 to 1. Use + - * / and brackets, and the functions avg, min, max, sum, mul and clamp (which pulls a value into 0…1).
ExerciseScore.unknownTests: No such test: {tests}. A misspelt name is not a syntax error — it is an exercise graded on something that does not exist.
ExerciseScore.unusedTests: Not used by the expression, so it counts for nothing: {tests}
ExerciseScore.isAnAverage: This expression is an average, so it can be turned back into weights without losing anything.

switchIn.done: The exercise now has custom scoring.
switchIn.noTests: Add a test first: an expression with nothing to refer to is not one UPolníček will store.

switchOut.done: The score is an average again.

structure.title: How it is wired
structure.explain: Boxes are operations; a variable is the wire between them. A box reads or writes a variable by naming it, so a port left unconnected is not an error UPolníček will report — it is simply a wire that is not there.
structure.preview: The pipeline as you are editing it
structure.variablesExplain: A wire, or a value the pipeline supplies itself. A value starting with $ is a hole an exercise fills in.

dangling.explain: UPolníček will accept this. It will simply not do what the missing wires would have done.
